By the time you're done with the first level, you will want to scream 'FOR THE EMPEROR!!' 

On paper, this seems like your standard third person shooter, there's bullets coming out of stuff, and there's regenerating shields, so all we need now is the cover, right?

... What do you mean there's no cover function? What do you mean that what cover there is, is fully destructible? What do you mean shields are depleted easilly? What do you mean I won't be shooting at stuff most of the time? What do you mean I have to wade in there and execute stuff to regain my non-regenerating health?

Welcome to Space Marine, where taking cover is HERESY, and where the best way of dealing with problems is to chop its head off or crush it with your BARE HANDS!

In the grimdark future of Warhammer 40K, there is only war. And it is glorious, fun to play, and a relief from the mediocrity of other third-person shooters with cover.

The game itself is beautifully done and personifies the Warhammer universe to a T. Also it would be nice to be able to play the "horde mode" with others.

Addendum: I do highly recomend getting the relevant DLC such as Chaos Unleashed. The rest is really a treat to yourself.

Secondary Addendum: The Campaign while short, shows quite a bit of what the Warhammer 40k Universe is about, from loyalist to cultist, The Imperiums Space Marines vs the Green Tide it is a truly stunning game.

The multiplayer itself isn't "fast paced" but at a decent enough speed so that anyone playing it will have a chance to come out in a decent light, even those on the losing team. But be warned, you WILL cuss every time you're in a close in fight and just barely lose. The silver lining? Jet Packs explode.

10 out of 10 for this highly underrated yet very fun game.

A well-crafted TPS game developed by Relic. Remember the trailer in which Lance Henriksen says he is a space marine? Gameplay-wise it is a very simple game: Titus, our protagonist, uses melee and ranged weapons alike to eliminate hordes of orcs attacking the marines. You also have a fury meter that is gradually filling up as you get rid of enemies. This allows you to unleash even stronger and deadlier attacks.

The game has excellent graphics, voice acting and sound effects. While the plot is not something we have not already seen elsewhere, it has its great moments. It is unfortunate that the planned sequels were cancelled as THQ went bankrupt.

I do not think multiplayer is played by anyone these days (after all, this is a 3-year old game), but as it is currently on sale (for 10 bucks) you can easily pick it up and spend some quality time with a squad full of ultramarines.

This is an absolutely amazing shooter, most especially for fans of the 40K.

The story is exceptional for a video game based so thoroughly in the visceral brutality of its combat, though it may seem straightforward and lacking in any new device for followers of the 40K fiction. 

At times the multiplayer on this was also fantastic, though long wait times and a lack of playerbase seems to have adversely impacted that.

Catch this on a good sale, or even pony up full price for a truly memorable and remarkable experience for fans and newcomers to the 40K world as well.
